pure-announcement.rationale: It documents an established scheduling algorithm and its Anki integration, not a launch, release or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: The vault's ebbinghaus-forgetting-curve concept covers the decay phenomenon and never mentions FSRS; an ML-optimized scheduler fitted to review history is new material for a reader of that note.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The algorithm's claims rest on two linked peer-reviewed Maimemo papers (KDD 2022, TKDE 2023) and open-source implementations anyone can run.

durability.rationale: The core — a two-part design where a scheduler applies the FSRS memory model and an optimizer fits its parameters to the user's own review history — is research-backed and shipped in Anki core since 23.10, so it will outlast the ephemeral add-on compatibility table.

actionability.rationale: The note's own actions are product steps and pointers — enable FSRS via the Anki manual, avoid interval-modifying add-ons, follow links to implementations — with the transferable mechanism detail living behind its references rather than in the note.

atomicity.rationale: It is one idea — data-driven spaced-repetition scheduling with per-user parameter optimization — stateable in a paragraph, with the compatibility matrix and acknowledgements as packaging.
